title: Bar in tension
description: Steel bar 100 x 20 x 10 mm, 20 kN along +x on the end x = 100. The faces x = 0, y = 0 and z = 0 are sliding supports (symmetry planes): they stop rigid-body motion but leave the lateral (Poisson) contraction free, so the stress is uniform right up to the support.

quantities.label: Axial stress at mid-length
quantities.citation: J. M. Gere, B. J. Goodno, Mechanics of Materials, 8th ed., Cengage 2013, Chapter 1, normal stress and strain
quantities.tolerance_reason: With sliding supports the uniform stress state is exact for any mesh, so a larger error means a wrong area, load or support.

quantities.label: Elongation (x movement of the loaded end)
quantities.citation: J. M. Gere, B. J. Goodno, Mechanics of Materials, 8th ed., Cengage 2013, Section 2.2, changes in lengths of axially loaded members
quantities.tolerance_reason: A linear displacement field is exact for quadratic elements; the band catches setup errors.
